feature: Icon previews at 32 and 48, with one dark chip
summary: A 24 point icon now shows at 16, 24, 32 and 48 beside the artboard, the way the icon mock draws it, and the 32 sits on a dark chip so you see the glyph on a dark ground too.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/icon-previews-dark-chip-walk.json.

try.do: Choose File > New Frame, pick 24 under Icons and click Add Frame.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and a circle inside the frame.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the row in the top left: 16, 24, 32 on dark, 48.
Change a shape's fill to black and look at the dark chip: the glyph turns light there.
Add a 16 point icon frame the same way.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Is the rule right: every size an icon is used at, up to twice the size you drew it at (so a 16 shows at 16, 24 and 32; a 32 or bigger shows all five, 16 to 64)?
Is the chip before the biggest the right one to make dark, or would you rather the dark chip were always 32?
Does turning a one colour dark glyph light on the dark chip read the way you expect a template icon to look in dark mode?
Does a coloured glyph (the red one here) on the dark chip tell you anything useful, or should the dark chip only appear for one colour glyphs?
rough: Matches icon-draw-wt.html step 11: 16, 24, 32 and 48 under a 24 point glyph, the 32 on the mock's own near black, and the glyph sitting straight on light chips painted the frame's own white.

Light chips still show exactly the exported picture. Leaving the white out of it was tried and measured: a thin line's soft edge then read up to a fifth darker on screen than in the file, which would hide the hairlines the strip is for.
Only a glyph drawn in one dark grey turns light on the dark chip. A coloured or many coloured icon is shown as drawn there, which is how it will really be seen.
The walk could not paint a shape black (no walk step reaches the colour well yet), so the light on dark case is proved by unit tests rather than in these pictures.
